winner_rationale:
WINNER: a merge, with PALIMPSEST as the spine. All three concepts converged on the same physical stack (falkordblite on TCP, laser-stack Log-only, one .pipe, four Guild agents, one OpenAPI bridge) — so the real choice was between three NARRATIVES and three PROOF STRATEGIES, and each won a different category.

Why Palimpsest wins the frame: it is the only concept whose domain sentence a judge understands in four seconds ("we remember what the internet overwrites") and whose central proof is an EXPERIMENT rather than an assertion. The REWIND A/B — replay the identical LaserData log from offset 0 into an empty graph key, same model, same prompt, opposite verdict — is the strongest possible answer to the only question these judges actually ask ("is the graph decorative?"), and it proves TWO sponsors with ONE mechanic, because durable ordered replay is the thing only LaserData can do. Nothing in the other two concepts beats it per unit of stage time.

Grafted from RINGLEADER: the concrete ring query. Palimpsest's "coordinated campaign" was hand-wavy; Ringleader specified the actual co-edit traversal (a:Actor)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(b)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(c) with ts-window and DISTINCT-actor constraints. That is what makes the cold-vs-warm verdicts differ for a MECHANICAL reason rather than an LLM mood — the difference between a demo and a coin flip. I also took Ringleader's hardest discipline verbatim: LaserData Log primitive ONLY, everything else gated behind await laser.capabilities(), which turns local-stack -> Cloud -> bare Iggy into a one-env-var swap instead of a rewrite. And gates that produce SAVED ARTIFACTS, not verbal green-lights.

Grafted from SECOND SHIFT (the schedule saver): the ONE-SPINE/FOUR-SURFACES move. Lifting unblock's 4-tuple _VERB_DISPATCH table means one artifact emits the MCP surface RocketRide's mcp_client mounts, the REST surface the UI eats, the OpenAPI 3.0 spec that becomes the SINGLE Guild integration, and a CLI for rehearsal. Guild's sandbox (no fetch, no npm, no Node built-ins) is the biggest schedule risk in this hackathon; three integrations would eat the sprint. This collapses it to one, and it is the difference between finishing and not. Second Shift's per-agent identity port (session_persona.py -> author_agent on every Cypher write) also comes across, because it is what turns "analyst contradicted watcher" from a caption into a queryable graph fact.

Rejected: Second Shift as the primary frame ("live operations desk" is abstract, judges cannot picture it, and there is no verifiable ground truth on stage), and Ringleader's name (ambiguous about who the ringleader is). Cut entirely: Palimpsest's write-back to test.wikipedia.org, and any use of laser.graph()/laser.memory() — both invite a judge to ask which layer is really the memory.

Decisive environment facts verified IN-SESSION today, which shaped the merge: the RocketRide engine is ALREADY BOOTED (PID 9858 on 127.0.0.1:5565); port 6399 is ALREADY HELD by a stray redis-server, so FalkorDB moves to 6401; Docker is NOT installed and the guild CLI is NOT installed; system python is 3.9.6. Two of four sponsors are therefore zero-risk and already running, one needs a 15-minute install on someone else's laptop, and one needs a human at a booth. The plan is shaped around exactly that asymmetry.

concept.name: PALIMPSEST — the sentinel that remembers what the internet overwrites
concept.pitch: Palimpsest watches the world's public knowledge being rewritten in real time and remembers every version as a directed, attributed property graph. A single edit is never suspicious; a coordinated campaign is — and Palimpsest catches the fourth move of a ring in one 3-hop Cypher query, in under five milliseconds, across entities that arrived at different times from different sources. Four specialist agents split the work, refuse to act without a human, and fire a real action with the full provenance chain attached. Then we prove the memory is load-bearing instead of claiming it: one keypress replays the identical event log from offset zero into an empty graph, and you watch the same agents, same model, same prompt, confidently make the wrong call. Kill the analyst mid-investigation and it restarts cold, reads its own handover node out of the graph, resumes from its committed stream offset, and finishes the case. Memory, visibly producing motion.

architecture:
ONE LAPTOP, SIX PROCESSES, ONE LOG SPINE, ONE DISPATCH TABLE. Everything on the critical path is localhost; only Guild's control plane needs the network.

[1] EDGE TAP — realtime/producer.py (~25 LOC). Holds an httpx SSE stream on Wikimedia EventStreams (https://stream.wikimedia.org/v2/stream/recentchange — zero-auth, verified live, 50-100 ev/s) and publishes every edit to LaserData topic `signal.raw` with key=wiki so per-wiki ordering survives parallel consumers. 4 partitions, batch_length=200, linger_ms=50, producer.init() BEFORE first send. A `--source file://demo/seed_replay.ndjson` flag drives the SAME code path from a 20-minute captured firehose, so conference wifi is never on the critical path. This is the only process that touches the public internet for ingest.

[2] LASERDATA PLANE — local laser-stack (iggy-server + laser-plane via Docker). Six topics: signal.raw, signal.salient, case.opened, case.decision, action.executed, agent.handoff. LaserData is the ONLY interface between services: every memory write, every RocketRide tool call, every Guild handoff, and every human ruling is a durable ordered record. Consumer group `graph-writers` with N members; the server assigns one partition per member and rebalances live on join/kill. auto_commit=disabled, commit-AFTER-side-effects-land. HARD SCOPE RULE: Log primitive ONLY. Views/Changes/State/Graph/Memory are never called, and every capability beyond Log is gated behind `await laser.capabilities()` — which is exactly what makes local-stack -> LaserData Cloud -> bare Apache Iggy a one-env-var swap.

[3] SENSING GATE — realtime/gate.py, between consumer and graph. Embeds the candidate edit summary, runs a FalkorDB vector KNN, drops the write if top-1 cosine DISTANCE is under threshold (0.15, ported from unblock's sensing-gate). Without it a 50-100 ev/s firehose turns the projector graph into an unreadable hairball in four minutes — and the visual IS the pitch. Judge-visible stat: "41,208 events ingested, 912 nodes — the gate rejected 97% as non-novel."

[4] MEMORY — FalkorDB, memory/. falkordblite EMBEDDED, forced onto TCP via serverconfig={'port':'6401','bind':'127.0.0.1'}. Port 6401, NOT 6379 and NOT 6399 — verified in-session today that a stray redis-server already holds 6399 on the build Mac, and a 6379 collision produces a false-green (client connects fine, then fails on GRAPH.QUERY). Zero Docker, zero daemon, zero network: this is the least-breakable layer in the stack, which is why it is the local-of-record.
  Two graph keys on one server: `palimpsest` (warm, the real memory) and `palimpsest_cold` (empty, the A/B target).
  Nodes: :Actor, :Page, :Wiki, :Event, :Entity, :Claim, :Case, :Agent, :Assertion, :Action.
  Edges: [:EDITED {ts,bytes,summary}], [:ON], derived [:CO_EDITED_WITH {window_s,count}], [:ABOUT], [:MENTIONS], [:IMPLICATES], [:AUTHORED], [:RELATES {relation}] over unblock's 6-value vocabulary (supports|contradicts|derived_from|supersedes|duplicates|references) stored GENUINELY DIRECTED, and [:HANDED_OFF_TO {handover_id,status,summary,in_flight,next_steps,blockers,checkpoint}].
  Indexes: range on Actor.name, Page.title, Case.id; HNSW vector on Claim.emb and Event.emb (dim 256, cosine) for hybrid GraphRAG entry.
  memory/graph_writer.py (consumer group graph-writers) does gate -> Cypher MERGE -> emit delta to the UI topic. NO LLM ON THE LIVE PATH — milliseconds, and nothing to hang on stage. GraphRAG-SDK is pre-bake ONLY (batch, finalize() exactly once, it is O(total graph size)).

[5] THE SPINE / BRIDGE — app/bridge/, FastAPI, built on unblock's 4-tuple _VERB_DISPATCH table with the ~35-LOC generic router. ONE table, FOUR surfaces, and this is the single decision that makes the sprint finishable:
  (a) REST — consumed by the UI and the seed script
  (b) MCP streamable-http — mounted into RocketRide via its mcp_client node
  (c) auto-generated OpenAPI 3.0 spec — becomes the ONE Guild Integration (Guild's sandbox bans fetch/npm/Node built-ins, so an Integration is the only legal door; three of them would eat the sprint)
  (d) CLI — rehearsal + gate-artifact capture
  Verbs: remember, relate, recall, ring, graph, stream_publish, stream_tail, stream_replay, act, handover_write, handover_read, ask. Every verb flows through ONE request chokepoint so retries, error envelopes, and headers live in one place.

[6] MOTION — RocketRide, motion/palimpsest.pipe. Engine ALREADY BOOTED on this box (PID 9858, 127.0.0.1:5565, dev key MYAPIKEY, MIT, self-hosted, no signup). Graph: webhook_1 -> question_1 -> agent_rocketride "Commander" (Wave planner, max_waves=12) with control-attached llm_anthropic (Claude Sonnet), memory_internal, tool_falkordb (host 127.0.0.1, port 6401, graph=palimpsest, allow_writes=true — a FIRST-PARTY FalkorDB node, so the agent itself chooses to call falkordb.get_schema then falkordb.query), tool_http_request (Discord webhook + GitHub API), mcp_client (our bridge), and a researcher sub-agent with its own llm_anthropic (Haiku) + memory_internal -> response_answers. Driven with ttl=0, pipelineTraceLevel="full", set_events(token,[task,summary,flow,output,sse]) so `thinking` frames stream into the UI as live narration. Our Python is ~40 lines; the orchestration is ~130 lines of .pipe JSON.

[7] COORDINATION — Guild.ai, agents/. Four published agents: watcher (LaserData ops on the bridge integration), analyst (FalkorDB ring/recall + claim extraction), responder (fires the action via /act -> RocketRide), and commander which imports the other three as auto-generated typed /tool sub-packages — that import IS the handoff, with Zod schemas inherited from the callee. commander runs task.gather([watcher, analyst]) for genuine parallel NOW-parallel-EVER, then ui_prompt BLOCKS for human approval (options + recommendation + timeoutSec + DEFAULT-ON-TIMEOUT, shape lifted from unblock's AskOpts), then delegates to responder. useWorkspaceAgents:false set EXPLICITLY (it defaults true, which makes coordination look accidental to a judge).

[8] IDENTITY — session_persona.py ported near-verbatim: one bridge process serves N distinct agent identities keyed on Mcp-Session-Id / per-request header, zero cross-bleed. Every Cypher write is stamped author_agent. This is what makes "agent A contradicted agent B" a graph fact rather than a caption.

[9] PROJECTOR UI — app/web/index.html. Single file, no build step, dark, projector-sized type. Four regions: LIVE GRAPH (force-directed canvas, nodes/edges streamed off the log, animated path highlight when the analyst traverses), AGENT LANE (Guild handoffs + RocketRide SSE thinking), CASE/ACTION panel (fired actions with clickable URLs), and the LaserData offset/lag strip. Plus a COLD | WARM split toggle for the replay A/B. The UI holds NO state — it is a pure projection of the log and the graph.

DATA FLOW (the mandated flow, executing literally): human edits a wiki page -> SSE -> LaserData signal.raw -> consumer group -> sensing gate -> FalkorDB MERGE (+ delta to UI) -> ring Cypher -> if ring_score > threshold, publish case.opened + POST the Guild trigger -> commander task.gather(watcher || analyst) -> analyst's 3-hop Cypher joins the live edit to the pre-baked historical corpus -> RocketRide Wave agent calls falkordb.get_schema + falkordb.query + tool_http_request in ONE parallel wave and decides escalate/dismiss -> ui_prompt -> human approves -> responder fires Discord + a GitHub issue -> the action is written BACK as (:Action)-[:RELATES {relation:'derived_from'}]->(:Event) so every action has clickable provenance -> UI renders. Every one of those arrows is a durable LaserData record.

sponsor_integration.falkordb:
ROLE: memory of record — and the layer that answers the question nothing else in the stack can express.

THREE LOAD-BEARING PROOFS, each with a removal test:
(1) THE RING QUERY. The escalate/dismiss verdict is computed from a single variable-length Cypher over a time window returning Path objects: MATCH p=(a:Actor)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(b:Actor)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(c:Actor) with ts-window and DISTINCT-actor constraints. Three accounts, four pages, twelve minutes — no individual edit crosses any threshold. We put run_time_ms (measured 2.45ms for 3 hops on this box) on screen next to the result. A vector store cannot express 'semantically similar to a four-step causal chain'.
(2) SUPERSEDE LINEAGE. MATCH p=(old:Claim{id:$id})<-[:RELATES*{relation:'supersedes'}]-(newest) WHERE NOT (newest)<-[:RELATES{relation:'supersedes'}]-() RETURN newest, length(p) — 'you told me X, then Y; here is the CURRENT truth and the chain that got there.' We also fix a real defect we inherited: unblock's contradiction_edges table has a block_id_a < block_id_b CHECK that forces DIRECTED relations to be stored UNDIRECTED (its own source comments flag it). We drop it, and say so: 'we improved on the production system we ported from.'
(3) HYBRID GraphRAG IN ONE QUERY. CALL db.idx.vector.queryNodes('Claim','emb',10,vecf32($q)) YIELD node AS seed MATCH (seed)-[:MENTIONS]->(e:Entity)<-[:MENTIONS]-(neighbor) — semantic entry, symbolic expansion, one round trip.

THE KILLER PROOF IS THE ABLATION, NOT THE CLAIM: identical event replayed twice from the same log, once into palimpsest and once into empty palimpsest_cold. Same model, same prompt, same agents. COLD -> 'Routine edit. No action.' WARM -> 'Coordinated campaign, 4th move. Escalate.' Both terminal outputs captured side by side as a saved gate artifact.

SECOND ROLE JUDGES DO NOT EXPECT: the agents' OWN continuity lives here. Findings, provenance, and the [:HANDED_OFF_TO {status:'open'}] handover nodes that make kill-and-resume work. So deleting FalkorDB also kills the demo's headline moment.

REMOVAL TEST: delete FalkorDB and there is no ring detection, no lineage, no attribution, no cold-resume, and the agent's decision measurably degrades on camera.

BOUNDARY WE STATE OUT LOUD: LaserData's SDK ships laser.graph() and laser.memory(). We deliberately do not call them. Laser is NOW plus the spine; FalkorDB is EVER.
sponsor_integration.rocketride:
ROLE: the execution layer. The .pipe file IS the orchestration, not a summarizer we call once.

THE DISQUALIFYING ANTI-PATTERN would be writing our own asyncio loop and calling RocketRide to phrase the answer. We do the inverse: the agent loop, tool selection, retries, parallel fan-out, and sub-agent delegation all live in motion/palimpsest.pipe (~130 lines of JSON). Our Python is ~40 lines of client — use() / send() / terminate() / SSE stream.

NON-REMOVABLE BECAUSE:
(a) FalkorDB is reached THROUGH RocketRide's first-party tool_falkordb node, not through a Python client. The trace shows the AGENT choosing to call falkordb.get_schema to learn the memory model, then falkordb.query with $params to recall, then falkordb.query with MERGE to write back. One wiring makes two sponsors load-bearing, via an integration RocketRide themselves built.
(b) agent_rocketride is their Wave planner: each wave it plans a BATCH of tool calls and runs them in PARALLEL. The live fetch (NOW) and the graph recall (EVER) execute in the SAME wave, then it decides. That is the hackathon's reference data flow executing literally, inside their engine, in one sentence.
(c) The other sponsors are mounted THROUGH RocketRide rather than beside it: mcp_client mounts our bridge's MCP surface as agent tools; tool_http_request fires the real-world action. One graph, four logos, nothing bolted on.

VISIBLE PROOF: pipelineTraceLevel='full' + set_events(token,['task','summary','flow','output','sse']) streams SSE type='thinking' frames ('Calling tool_falkordb...', 'LLM call started') into the AGENT LANE panel, so judges watch the orchestration narrate itself. Gate artifact: a screenshot of a single wave containing 2+ parallel tool calls.

REMOVAL TEST: delete the .pipe and nothing in our repo selects a tool. Delete just the tool_falkordb node and the agent loses the ability to decide.

RISK POSTURE: lowest external risk in the stack. MIT, self-hosted, no signup, no key hunt (built-in dev key MYAPIKEY), and the engine is ALREADY BOOTED on the build Mac at 127.0.0.1:5565 with a two-node pipeline verified end to end.
sponsor_integration.guild:
ROLE: the agent organization, the type contract between specialists, and the human gate. HIGHEST-RISK SPONSOR, so the entire architecture is shaped to de-risk it.

NON-REMOVABLE BY CONSTRUCTION:
(a) DELEGATION IS TYPED AND RUNTIME-DISPATCHED. Every published agent auto-generates a /tool sub-package at publish time; commander imports @guildai/<owner>~analyst/tool and inherits its Zod input/output schemas. Delete Guild and the three specialists lose their tool surface, the handoffs lose their contracts, and every agent collapses into one undifferentiated process.
(b) task.gather([watcherTool(...), analystTool(...)]) is the parallel NOW-and-EVER fan-out — and it is BRANDED to tool-call expressions only, so it genuinely is Guild's runtime doing the concurrency, not Promise.all.
(c) ui_prompt BLOCKS for human approval before any consequential action, carrying options + recommendation + timeoutSec + default-on-timeout (shape lifted from unblock's AskOpts). That is the human-in-the-loop leg of the mandate, first-class.
(d) THE SANDBOX FORCES IT. Guild agent code may import only @guildai/agents-sdk, zod, and @guildai-services/* — no fetch, no npm, no Node built-ins. So every external system reaches our agents ONLY through a Guild Integration with server-side credential injection; agent code never sees a raw key. The delegation contract is enforced by the runtime, not by convention.
(e) THE VERIFIABLE ARTIFACT: `guild session events <session-id>` prints a real server-side trace — commander -> analyst -> ui_prompt -> responder — with per-agent identities, tool calls, token counts, and credential scopes. We hand judges the session id. That is a coordination receipt, not a screenshot of an import statement. It also spans the kill: the trace shows one agent dying and another resuming the same case.

THE SCHEDULE-DEFINING DECISION: ONE thin FastAPI bridge exposing FalkorDB + LaserData + RocketRide behind ONE OpenAPI 3.0 spec = ONE integration instead of three. And the spec is written and published FIRST (hour 1-2), before the bridge is finished, so the six-step create -> version create -> operation create --openapi -> build -> publish -> connect cycle runs in PARALLEL with implementation.

FORCED SEQUENCING (platform, not preference): specialists published FIRST (the /tool package only exists after publish), orchestrator LAST, and specialist Zod schemas FROZEN at the H0:30 contract freeze because every change costs republish + npm install + rebuild.

REMOVAL TEST: delete Guild and the three sponsor integrations lose their tool surface, the handoffs lose their type contracts, and the human approval gate disappears entirely.
sponsor_integration.laserdata:
ROLE: the nervous system — and we make it the ONLY interface between services, so it is architecture rather than an import, and unfalsifiable to a judge.

HONEST FRAMING WE SAY UNPROMPTED, BEFORE ANYONE ASKS: LaserData does not supply data, it moves it. We bring the source (Wikimedia's zero-auth public firehose); LaserData carries, orders, durably stores, partitions, and replays it. Saying that out loud reads as rigor, not weakness.

FOUR LOAD-BEARING PROOFS:
(1) REPLAY AS THE PROOF ITSELF — our single strongest beat. The cold-vs-warm A/B is IMPLEMENTED as a durable replay: a fresh consumer at polling='first' from offset 0 re-derives the entire graph from scratch into the empty palimpsest_cold key in seconds. 'Watch me rewind and re-derive the memory' is the literal embodiment of memory meets motion, and no other sponsor in the stack can do it. One mechanic, two sponsors, zero hand-waving. We also assert node/edge digests match the live-built graph.
(2) CONSUMER GROUPS AS THE AGENT SUBSTRATE. graph-writers has N members; the server assigns one partition per member and rebalances live. We kill a member on stage and show partitions redistribute with zero coordinator and zero message loss (committed offsets asserted before and after). key=wiki preserves per-entity ordering across the whole team.
(3) CRASH-SAFETY IS THE DEMO. auto_commit=disabled with commit-after-side-effects means the kill-and-resume beat resumes from the exact committed offset. Delete LaserData and cold-restart loses its 'motion' half — FalkorDB only restores the 'memory' half. Both mandated layers are structurally required for the headline trick.
(4) EVERY ACTION IS A RECORD. Memory writes, RocketRide tool calls, Guild handoffs, and human rulings all publish to the six topics. 'Every tool call this system ever made is on the log and I can replay any of them' is true, not aspirational.

CORRECTNESS: our consumer ports unblock's four hard-won streaming invariants verbatim (enqueue-before-ack, dedup on stream sequence NOT message_id, backpressure-not-drop, cancellation-safe teardown). Delivery is at-least-once by design, so every graph write is a MERGE and every action record is keyed by case_id + decision_hash.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: Log primitive only. Views/Changes/State/Graph/Memory are never called; everything beyond Log is gated behind await laser.capabilities(). That is what makes the fallback ladder a one-env-var swap rather than a rewrite — and it keeps laser.graph()/laser.memory() from cannibalizing FalkorDB's mandated role.

REMOVAL TEST: two commands. Stop the plane and all six processes stop exchanging; there is no replay, no crash recovery, no audit trail. The system does not start.

fallbacks.falkordb: LOWEST RISK — this is the local-of-record and it is already proven on the build Mac. TIER 1 (primary): falkordblite embedded, `from redislite.falkordb_client import FalkorDB` (NOT `import falkordblite`), py3.12, serverconfig={'port':'6401','bind':'127.0.0.1'} — verified today: cross-process standard-client connect, 3-hop [*1..3] traversal in 2.45ms, HNSW index + db.idx.vector.queryNodes, cross-session persistence. Zero Docker, zero network. TIER 2: Docker server on whichever laptop has Docker — buys the falkordb-browser visualizer on :3000 for free (bind 127.0.0.1 only, and MOUNT THE VOLUME: `docker run --rm` without -v loses the entire graph on restart). TIER 3: FalkorDB Cloud free tier as the shared cross-laptop mirror (no TLS, no backups — nothing sensitive in it). THE REAL RISK IS PORT DISCIPLINE, NOT AVAILABILITY: 6399 is ALREADY HELD by a stray redis-server on the build Mac (verified in-session), and starting a second Lite instance there fails with `RedisLiteServerStartError: The redis-server process failed to start`, which says nothing about ports and would burn 45 minutes at 2am. 6379 is worse — FalkorDB speaks the Redis protocol, so a stray redis-server lets you CONNECT and then fails on GRAPH.QUERY, a textbook false green. We bind 6401, `lsof -i :6401` is step one of every debug, and host/port/graph-name/db-path live in ONE shared constant at memory/config.py because falkordblite persistence is per-FILE-PATH and two teammates on different paths silently fork with no error. IF EVERYTHING FAILS: pre-snapshot demo/palimpsest.db and run the demo read-only off the snapshot.

demo_script:
90 SECONDS. Roles fixed in advance and rehearsed: DEV B DRIVES (sole hand on the keyboard, never speaks). DEV C NARRATES (never touches a key). DEV A HOLDS THE PHONE. One projector, one browser window, four regions already live, firehose pre-warmed 45+ minutes so the graph is dense and the actor has genuine history. Everything runs on localhost.

[0:00-0:10] HOOK — no slide, no title card. The screen is ALREADY ALIVE: nodes landing on the LIVE GRAPH every fraction of a second, offsets climbing on the bottom strip.
DEV C: "This is Wikipedia being rewritten, right now. Fifty edits a second, worldwide. Every node arriving is a real person editing a real page in the last few seconds. A single edit is never suspicious. A campaign is."

[0:10-0:22] IT IS REAL, AND YOU CAN CHECK IT YOURSELF — Dev A holds up the phone, visibly types, hits save on a Wikipedia sandbox page. Within ~2 seconds a new node blooms on the projector, ringed and labelled with the editor name.
DEV C: "That went from his phone, through Wikimedia's public firehose, through LaserData, into our graph. Sub-second. Zero auth — pull out your own phone after this and verify the feed." (This beat is a human action WE perform. No beat in this demo depends on chance.)
Point at the gate counter: "41,208 events ingested. 912 nodes. The salience gate rejected the rest as non-novel. This is memory, not a log dump."

[0:22-0:40] THE MONEY SHOT — THREE HOPS. The analyst wakes on that node. An animated path traces across the canvas, lighting four nodes in sequence, ending deep in a differently-coloured cluster. The Cypher and run_time_ms: 2.45 drop into the panel, large.
DEV C: "Three accounts, four pages, twelve minutes. No individual edit crosses any threshold. One three-hop Cypher query over everything that ever happened — two milliseconds. A vector store cannot even express that question; there is no such thing as 'semantically similar to a four-step causal chain.'"

[0:40-0:52] THE PROOF — THE REWIND. This is the beat that wins. Dev B hits ONE key. The screen splits COLD | WARM.
DEV C: "Same events. Same model. Same prompt. Same agents. On the right, our memory. On the left, I am replaying the identical LaserData log from offset zero into an empty graph."
The cold panel builds in fast-forward; both verdicts land side by side — COLD: "Routine edit. No action." WARM: "Coordinated campaign, fourth move. Escalate."
DEV C: "That is the whole thesis. Delete the memory and the same agents make the wrong call. It is not decoration — it is the difference between those two answers. And only a durable ordered log lets you feed the exact same reality to two different agents."

[0:52-1:08] COORDINATION, A HUMAN, AND A REAL ACTION. The AGENT LANE scrolls the live Guild trace: commander -> gather(watcher || analyst) -> analyst returns -> ui_prompt. A card appears: "Escalate this campaign? [approve] [dismiss] — auto-dismiss in 20s."
DEV C, turning the laptop toward the judges: "Four Guild agents. The commander called two of them in parallel — what's happening now, and what ever happened — and then it stopped for a person. It will not act without one."
A judge or Dev A taps APPROVE. The ACTION LOG fills: a Discord message posts on screen, a GitHub issue URL appears.
DEV C: "Real action, real world, full provenance attached — every memory that caused it and which agent asserted it. Open that URL on your phone."

[1:08-1:22] THE FINALE — MEMORY MEETS MOTION, LITERALLY. Dev B kills the analyst mid-investigation: pkill -f analyst. The lane goes dead. He restarts it cold — no arguments, no state, no context.
DEV C: "Watch." — It reads its own open handover node out of FalkorDB, re-attaches to its LaserData consumer group at its last committed offset, honours the approval it never personally received, and finishes the case on screen.
DEV C: "We killed it. It remembered what it was doing — from the graph — and it remembered where it was — from the log. It didn't restart. It resumed."

[1:22-1:30] CLOSE.
DEV C: "Every fact attributed to the agent that asserted it. Every action replayable from offset zero. Every handoff durable enough to survive the agent that made it. LaserData carried it, FalkorDB remembered it, RocketRide decided, Guild coordinated it — and asked us first. That's Palimpsest."
Leave the graph canvas running.

SIX Q&A TERMINALS PRE-LOADED ON A SPARE DESKTOP: (1) guild session events <id> — read the coordination trace yourself. (2) the .pipe file — 130 lines of RocketRide JSON against 40 lines of our Python. (3) mcp_smoke.py — watch a tool fire live, nothing is mocked. (4) the supersede-lineage query — the answer to "why not a vector DB". (5) the LaserData two-command falsification. (6) plan/LOAD_BEARING.md with all four removal tests.

HARD RULES: the entire 90 seconds runs from ONE terminal script and ONE browser tab. A full screen capture recorded at T+6:45 is one keystroke away. If any live element misbehaves we CUT TO TAPE AND KEEP NARRATING — we never debug on stage. CUT ORDER if long, agreed at hour -1: kill-and-resume first, then judge-taps-approve (Dev A taps instead), then the hybrid vector query. NEVER the rewind.

judge_qa.q: Is FalkorDB actually load-bearing, or is it a key-value store in a graph costume?
judge_qa.a: Run the ablation in front of you — it takes eight seconds. Identical event, replayed from the same log into two graph keys: warm returns 'coordinated campaign, escalate,' cold returns 'routine edit, dismiss.' Same model, same prompt, same agents. The verdict is computed from a variable-length Cypher co-edit traversal — (a:Actor)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(b)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(c) — returning Path objects in 2.45ms. Delete FalkorDB and there is no ring detection, no supersede lineage, no attribution, and no cold-resume, because the agents' own handover state lives in the graph too. We also improved on the production system we ported the model from: unblock's edge table has a block_id_a < block_id_b CHECK that forces directed relations to be stored undirected. We dropped it; ours are genuinely directed.

judge_qa.q: Why not just a vector database, or Postgres with a recursive CTE?
judge_qa.a: Two questions we answer that neither can express. First, the ring: 'semantically similar to a four-step causal chain across distinct actors within a twelve-minute window' is not a vector operation — there is no embedding of a path. Second, supersede-lineage: MATCH p=(old)<-[:RELATES*{relation:'supersedes'}]-(newest) WHERE NOT (newest)<-[:RELATES{relation:'supersedes'}]-() resolves current truth from a revision chain of unknown depth in one shot. A CTE can do the second with real effort; neither does the third thing, which is our hybrid GraphRAG query — db.idx.vector.queryNodes for semantic entry, then symbolic expansion through shared :Entity nodes, in ONE round trip. We use the vector index; we just do not stop there.

judge_qa.q: What did LaserData actually give you? You brought your own data.
judge_qa.a: We say this before you ask: LaserData does not supply data, it moves it. We bring Wikimedia's public firehose; LaserData carries, orders, partitions, durably stores, and replays it. And it is the ONLY interface between our six services — every memory write, every tool call, every handoff, every human ruling is a log record. Two commands falsify it: stop the plane and nothing exchanges. But the real proof is that our strongest beat IS a LaserData primitive — the cold-vs-warm A/B is implemented as a durable replay from offset 0, and only an ordered durable log lets you feed the exact same reality to two different agents. We also kill a consumer-group member on stage and show partitions rebalance with zero coordinator and zero message loss, with committed offsets asserted before and after.

judge_qa.q: Isn't Guild just four imports? Couldn't you do this with a Python script?
judge_qa.a: Read the trace, don't take my word: guild session events <id> is a server-side record showing commander -> analyst -> ui_prompt -> responder with per-agent identities, tool calls, token counts, and credential scopes. Three structural things a script does not give you. One: delegation is TYPED and runtime-dispatched — the /tool sub-package is generated at publish time and the caller inherits the callee's Zod schemas. Two: task.gather is branded to tool-call expressions only, so the parallel now-and-ever fan-out is genuinely Guild's runtime, not Promise.all. Three: the sandbox bans fetch, npm, and Node built-ins, so every external system reaches our agents only through a Guild Integration with server-side credential injection — agent code never sees a raw key. Agents are independent security principals. That is the answer to 'why not a script.'

judge_qa.q: Did you write the orchestration yourself and just call RocketRide once to summarize?
judge_qa.a: The exact opposite, and the file counts prove it: the orchestration is ~130 lines of motion/palimpsest.pipe JSON; our Python is ~40 lines of client — connect, use, send, stream. The agent loop, tool selection, retries, parallel fan-out, and sub-agent delegation all live in their engine. Delete the .pipe and NOTHING in our repo selects a tool. And watch the trace: the agent chose to call falkordb.get_schema to learn our memory model, then composed parameterized Cypher itself, through RocketRide's own first-party tool_falkordb node. That is a vendor-built integration, not glue we invented.

judge_qa.q: Show me the parallel execution you keep claiming.
judge_qa.a: Here — pipelineTraceLevel='full' with set_events([task,summary,flow,output,sse]). This is one Wave from the agent_rocketride planner containing two tool calls dispatched in the same batch: the live fetch and the graph recall, then the decision. That is the hackathon's reference flow — what's happening now plus what ever happened, then decide — executing as engine primitives rather than as our for-loop.

judge_qa.q: What is actually novel here versus a RAG chatbot?
judge_qa.a: Three things. One: the decision is a function of a TRAVERSAL, not a retrieval — and we prove it by ablation rather than claiming it. Two: every fact is attributed to the agent that asserted it, so contradictions between agents are directed edges in the graph, not prose, and a human breaks the tie before anything fires. Three: continuity survives the process. Kill the agent and it resumes from a handover node plus a committed stream offset — memory restoring what it knew, the log restoring where it was. A RAG chatbot has none of those; it re-retrieves and starts over.

judge_qa.q: What if the conference wifi dies right now?
judge_qa.a: Nothing on the critical path needs it. falkordblite is embedded on 127.0.0.1:6401 — no Docker, no daemon; laser-stack is local; the RocketRide engine is local and MIT-licensed with a built-in dev key. Only Guild's control plane is remote, and we drilled that segment against tape. Every service takes --offline and replays a captured 20-minute firehose through the identical code path, so the file source and the live source are literally the same code. We rehearsed the whole 90 seconds with wifi physically off.

judge_qa.q: How do I know any of this is real and not mocked?
judge_qa.a: Four handles, all live on that spare desktop. mcp_smoke.py calls a bridge tool in front of you right now. guild session events is a server-side trace whose rendering we do not control. The GitHub issue we just filed is a public URL — open it on your phone. And the Wikimedia firehose is zero-auth: curl https://stream.wikimedia.org/v2/stream/recentchange from your own laptop and watch the same events we're consuming.

judge_qa.q: Your stack has overlapping capabilities — LaserData ships its own graph and memory primitives. Which layer is really the memory?
judge_qa.a: We noticed that too, and we deliberately do not call laser.graph() or laser.memory(). Hard rule, stated in the README: LaserData owns 'what is happening now' plus the message spine; FalkorDB owns 'what ever happened.' Using both would muddy both sponsor stories and make it fair to ask you which one is decorative. We also use ONLY LaserData's Log primitive and gate everything else behind await laser.capabilities() — which is why the same code runs unchanged on local stack, their Cloud, or bare Apache Iggy.

judge_qa.q: Which model built the graph, and what happens when it's slow or rate-limited?
judge_qa.a: Claude, via LiteLLM in GraphRAG-SDK, for the pre-baked historical corpus — and here's the ontology it invented for itself from the raw documents. But there is ZERO LLM on the live path: streaming ingest is raw parameterized Cypher MERGE, milliseconds, nothing to hang. The LLM only runs inside the RocketRide decision loop with capped waves. We made that split deliberately, because GraphRAG ingest is an LLM call per chunk and finalize() is O(total graph size) — calling it in a streaming loop gets quadratically slower on stage.

judge_qa.q: How do you keep a 50-100 event/second firehose from turning the graph into noise?
judge_qa.a: A salience gate ported from a production system, running BEFORE every write: embed the candidate, run a vector KNN against the graph, and skip the MERGE if the nearest neighbour is closer than 0.15. That number on screen — 41,208 events in, 912 nodes kept — is the gate rejecting 97% as non-novel. Without it the ring query drowns in near-duplicates in about four minutes, and we found that out at hour 1, not on stage.

judge_qa.q: What would you do with another day?
judge_qa.a: Three things, in order. Narrow the ring detector from co-edit topology to timing-correlation scoring so it generalizes past Wikipedia. Make the contradiction resolution learn from human rulings — right now the ruling lands as a supersedes edge but nothing tunes the threshold from it. And harden attestation: we deliberately ship NO trust badge today, because the system we ported patterns from has attestation flags that are false in production with a live forgery path, and we would rather show you nothing than show you a hardcoded green checkmark.

risks.risk: #1 SCHEDULE KILLER — GUILD ACCOUNT PROVISIONING IS DEMO-GATED AND HAS NO ENGINEERING WORKAROUND. guild.ai's only CTA is 'Book a demo', there is no confirmed self-serve signup or public pricing, @guildai/agents-sdk is NOT on public npm (hard 404), and `guild agent init` exits with 'Not authenticated' and creates nothing. Without accounts an entire MANDATORY sponsor is zeroed. Compounding it: login needs a real browser round-trip (no --no-browser flag in v0.17.0), and trigger API keys can only be minted in the web UI. The guild CLI is not even installed on the build Mac yet.
risks.mitigation: Four layers. (0) PREVENTION: Dev C emails AND Discords the sponsor rep the night before for 3 org seats. (1) Dev C physically walks to the Guild booth at minute 0:00, before anyone opens an editor — this is action #1 for the entire team. (2) HARD GATE at T+60 with a LOUD escalation to organizers, not silent absorption, and an immediate branch. (3) FALLBACK LADDER: useWorkspaceAgents:true dynamic discovery (skips the entire publish -> /tool -> npm -> rebuild cycle, still produces a real handoff trace) -> drive Guild through `guild api` + the `guild mcp` stdio server -> total loss means RocketRide's researcher sub-agent + mcp_client carry the multi-agent story and our bridge's `ask` verb carries the human gate, stated honestly on stage rather than faked.

risks.risk: #2 GUILD'S SANDBOX MULTIPLIES AND SERIALIZES THE WORK. Agent code may import only @guildai/agents-sdk, zod, and @guildai-services/* — no fetch, no npm, no Node built-ins. So EVERY external system costs a full six-step OpenAPI create -> version create -> operation create -> build -> publish -> connect cycle. Three integrations would eat the sprint. Worse, it is SERIALIZED: the orchestrator literally cannot import a specialist until that specialist is published, and every specialist schema change forces republish + npm install + rebuild.
risks.mitigation: Solved ARCHITECTURALLY, and it is the single biggest de-risk in the plan: ONE FastAPI bridge, built on unblock's 4-tuple dispatch table, exposes FalkorDB + LaserData + RocketRide behind ONE auto-generated OpenAPI 3.0 spec = ONE integration. The spec is written and PUBLISHED FIRST at hour 1-2, before the bridge is finished, so the long-pole cycle runs in parallel with implementation. Sequencing is forced and pre-agreed: specialists published first with Zod schemas FROZEN at the H0:30 contract freeze, orchestrator last. The same table also emits the MCP surface RocketRide mounts and the REST surface the UI eats — one artifact, four consumers.

risks.risk: #3 SILENT-FAILURE TRAPS THAT PRESENT AS 'NO DATA' RATHER THAN AN ERROR — the class that kills demos at 2am because there is no stack trace to chase. (a) FalkorDB's vector score is a DISTANCE not a similarity (verified: 0.0 identical, 0.0061 neighbour) — sorting DESC shows judges the WORST matches while looking perfectly functional. (b) A stray redis-server on 6379 lets a client CONNECT and then fail on GRAPH.QUERY — a textbook false green — and 6399 is ALREADY OCCUPIED on the build Mac, where a second Lite instance fails with RedisLiteServerStartError that says nothing about ports. (c) falkordblite persistence is per-FILE-PATH: two teammates on different paths silently fork with no error. (d) unblock's handover reader returns an envelope, so a naive truthiness check treats a genuine MISS as a HIT. (e) GraphRAG-SDK's text-to-Cypher swallows ALL exceptions and returns empty. (f) The graph starts EMPTY, and a multi-hop query on an empty graph returns [] on stage.
risks.mitigation: Every one is pre-registered IN WRITING before anyone types, in memory/SCHEMA.md and motion/PIPE_NOTES.md. Concretely: bind 6401 and make `lsof -i :6401` step one of every debug; host/port/graph-name/db-path in ONE committed constant at memory/config.py; an assert-on-ordering unit test for the vector path at hour 1; explicit envelope unwrap plus a status=='open' guard on the handover read; text-to-Cypher stays OFF and off the critical path (enable_cypher=False is the default and it is experimental); 200-400 deterministic seed blocks + one synthetic ring landed by hour 1 as an explicit Gate-2 exit criterion; and every demo-critical query carries a non-empty assertion in the rehearsal script.

risks.risk: #4 THREE OF THE FOUR SDKs ARE EFFECTIVELY BRAND NEW AND THE DOCS WILL LIE TO YOU. laser-sdk shipped 0.0.1 on 2026-08-02 — the day before the event, ~544 total downloads, near-zero StackOverflow. @guildai/cli 0.17.0 shipped 2026-07-21. RocketRide's docs site LAGS the shipped 1.3.0 package and its CHANGELOG contradicts the installed code. Our composite .pipe has never run as a unit and tool_falkordb is marked experimental. On top of that the system python here is 3.9.6, where `pip install rocketride` SILENTLY installs 1.0.0 — a materially different API — instead of failing, and falkordblite's import path is `from redislite.falkordb_client import FalkorDB`, not its package name.
risks.mitigation: Trust the INSTALLED PACKAGE over the docs — introspect with inspect.signature rather than reading. Freeze all four SDK versions in a lockfile pre-event and upgrade NOTHING during the sprint. One pinned py3.12 venv baked into every run script so nobody ever types a bare pip install, plus a 60-second preflight that asserts versions and import paths before anyone debugs anything else. Use the connection string ./scripts/up PRINTS (iggy:laser@), never the examples' hardcoded iggy:iggy@. Build the .pipe UP node-by-node from the already-verified two-node baseline with client.validate() at every step, and keep the minimal pipe as a hot fallback. GATE 3 at T+3:00 exists specifically to fail the tool_falkordb assumption early, while there is still time to route around it via mcp_client. RocketRide's Discord stays open all day.

risks.risk: #5 DEMO-DAY FRAGILITY AND SCOPE CREEP — the two things that kill more hackathon demos than bugs. Conference wifi at Frontier Tower dies mid-pitch. A rare live event never fires during the 90 seconds and there is dead air. The firehose at 50-100 ev/s floods the canvas into an unreadable hairball — and the visual IS the pitch. `docker run --rm` without a volume loses the entire graph on restart, and the Docker one-liner binds 6379/3000 to ALL interfaces with no auth, which on conference wifi is an open writable database. And at 6:30 somebody has a beautiful new idea that destroys a working demo.
risks.mitigation: NOTHING ON STAGE DEPENDS ON CHANCE OR THE NETWORK. The trigger is a human action WE perform (a Wikipedia sandbox edit from Dev A's phone, sub-second, rehearsed three times) — we explicitly rejected an earthquake feed for this reason. Every service takes --offline and replays a captured 20-minute firehose through the identical code path; the whole 90 seconds was rehearsed with wifi physically off. Density is rehearsed against 45 MINUTES of accumulated data, not two, because hairball problems are invisible on a fresh graph — and the ported sensing gate at 0.15 plus k-hop-neighbourhood-only rendering keeps it readable. Mount the volume; bind 127.0.0.1 everywhere. Against scope creep: nothing new starts after GATE 5 at T+5:00, absolute feature freeze at 6:30, code freeze and tag at 7:00, a full backup screen capture recorded at 6:45 while everything works, and a CUT ORDER agreed at hour -1 — kill-and-resume -> judge-taps-approve -> hybrid vector query, never the rewind A/B — so nobody argues at 7:35.

runner_up_grafts: FROM RINGLEADER — the concrete ring query. Palimpsest's 'coordinated campaign' was hand-wavy; Ringleader specified the actual co-edit traversal (a:Actor)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(b)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(c) with ts-window and DISTINCT-actor constraints. This is what makes the cold-vs-warm verdicts differ for a MECHANICAL reason rather than an LLM mood — the difference between a demo and a coin flip.

FROM RINGLEADER — LaserData Log-primitive-ONLY discipline, with everything beyond Log gated behind await laser.capabilities(). This single constraint turns the fallback ladder (local laser-stack -> Cloud -> bare Apache Iggy) into a one-env-var swap instead of a rewrite, and it is the smartest portability call any of the three concepts made.

FROM RINGLEADER — gates produce SAVED ARTIFACTS in plan/gates/, not verbal green-lights. Judges verify usage; we hand them receipts: two terminal outputs side by side, a Wave screenshot, a session-id transcript, a node/edge digest match.

FROM RINGLEADER — the pre-registered payload-builder bug class (unblock_ingest's silent 400: tool speaks {utterances:[...]}, backend speaks {items:[...]}) and the mcp>=1.28,<2 pin rationale. Both are cheap tests that prevent expensive mysteries.

FROM SECOND SHIFT — THE SPINE. One 4-tuple dispatch table lifted from unblock's server.py generating FOUR surfaces (MCP + REST + OpenAPI + CLI) from one artifact. This is the schedule-defining move: it collapses Guild's three-integration problem to one, and it is the reason the bridge can ship by hour 2 instead of hour 5.

FROM SECOND SHIFT — per-agent identity via session_persona.py, stamping author_agent on every Cypher write. Neither of the other concepts made attribution structural. Without it, 'analyst asserted X, watcher contradicted it' is a caption; with it, it is a queryable graph fact rendered as node colour, and the contradiction beat becomes verifiable.

FROM SECOND SHIFT — the roster.json toolset-scoping manifest, giving watcher/analyst/responder narrowed, NON-OVERLAPPING tool surfaces from one file. This is also what makes the guild session events trace readable to a judge: each agent visibly owns a different sponsor.

FROM SECOND SHIFT — the explicit REMOVAL TEST per sponsor, written verbatim into the README and plan/LOAD_BEARING.md. Reframing every integration claim as a falsifiable deletion ('delete X and Y provably stops working') is what converts four logos into four load-bearing dependencies in a judge's notebook.

FROM PALIMPSEST (kept as the spine) — the rewind A/B as the primary proof; the phone-edit verification beat (a human action we perform, never a chance event); the two-graph-key design (palimpsest / palimpsest_cold); and the honest-framing discipline: say out loud, unprompted, that LaserData moves data rather than supplying it, and that we deliberately do not call laser.graph()/laser.memory().

DEDUPLICATED ACROSS ALL THREE — the shared reuse core every concept independently identified, kept in full: the sensing gate at threshold 0.15 (best effort-to-value ratio in the list), the four monitor.py streaming invariants, the handover schema with its two documented traps, the AskOpts default-on-timeout field, and the relate-verb relation vocabulary minus its undirected-storage CHECK constraint.
